en: The Dharani of the Wish-Fulfilling Mani Wheel for the Recitation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Baosiwei by Imperial Decree.
The Root Mantra is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya* (2) *Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya* (3–6) *Tadyathā* (7) *Oṃ* (8) *Cakrāvalī* (9) *Cintāmaṇi* (10) *Mahāpārśva* (11) *Milurutiṣṭha* (12–14) *Pracaṇḍa* (15) *Akarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ* (16–17) *Svāhā* (18). If there are sons or daughters of good family who uphold and recite this mantra:
If one begins the recitation each morning at dawn by chewing on a willow branch,
and completes one hundred thousand recitations of this mantra,
the Holy Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra will manifest in person and grant whatever boons are sought.
In reciting this mantra,
there is no distinction between those living at home and those who have left the household life; even those who drink alcohol, eat meat, or have wives and children—
provided they merely recite this mantra, they will certainly achieve accomplishment.
One who recites this mantra need not perform ritual procedures;
they need not observe fasts on previous days,
nor need they maintain a vegetarian diet.
There is no need for bathing,
nor is there a need for special clothing;
merely by reciting it, all shall be accomplished.
As explained at length in the sūtra:
for the root mudrā,
first join the palms and slightly bend the two middle fingers.
Place the tips of the two index fingers together.
With the two thumbs held side by side and pointing straight upward against the heart,
recite seven times and scatter [the water] over the crown of the head.
If there is an invocation,
move the two thumbs back and forth;
by the power of this mantra and mudrā, [the deities will arrive].
One's own person is identical to the majestic power and spiritual authority of the deity;
thus, no powerful māras can find an opportunity.
Next, the heart-mantra is as follows:
Oṃ padma-jvālā-maṇi-prabhā hūṃ. Next, the mantra according to the heart [of the deity] is as follows:
Recite "Oṃ va-rā-dha-pa-tte-me. Then, with the right hand inverted over the left, press the tip of the right little finger against the tip of the left thumb.
Press the tip of the right thumb against the tip of the left little finger.
The mantra is:

Oṃ ārya Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitāye bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā oṃ cchele cchele mahācchele cchele cchele cchele cchele dhāra svāhā. Recite this mantra three times while performing the mudrā and scatter it over the crown of the head.

The Dharani and Mudra for the Method of Protecting the Body and Establishing the Boundary of Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara: For this rite, use both hands to interlace the three fingers from the middle finger downward, turning them outward;
then, with the palms pressed against the backs of the hands, join them together in the *añjali* mudrā.
The two index fingers are held upright, separated by a distance of about five *aṅgula*,
with both thumbs pressed together;
each thumb is bent at one joint so as not to touch the tips of the index fingers while moving back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ pravicāsta vajra śrī svāhā. This is the seal of the Great Dharma-body of Hayagrīva: interlace the three fingers from the index finger downward with the palms facing outward.
Rotate each fingertip toward the back of the hand and join the palms.
Hold the two little fingers together, standing them upright and touching at their tips.
Bring the two thumbs together and bend them slightly, moving them back and forth in an angry manner.
The mantra is:

Oṃ (1) duna duna (2) moha moha (3) khāda khāda khāda hana gṛhṇa (5) huṃ svāhā (7). The Dharma-body mudrā of Hayagrīva: Interlace the four fingers of both hands, starting from the index fingers, with the palms facing outward.
Place each hand on the back of the head with the palms joined;
touch the two thumbs together and bend one joint of each,
ensuring the thumbs do not touch the index fingers as they move back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ svāhā. Next, perform the boundary-binding (sīmābandha) using the seal of Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara to ward off and eliminate obstructing spirits.
Join the two palms; bend the two index fingers and the two ring fingers into the palms so that they face each other's backs.
Place both thumbs side by side, slightly bent, without touching the index fingers.
Then recite the mantra of Hayagrīva as follows:
Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Recite this three times and immediately rotate the mudrā three times counter-clockwise.
All māras are warded off and driven away, dispersing of their own accord.
By circling the mudrā three times to the right,
a firm and great boundary is immediately established.
The aforementioned method for protecting the body also employs the Bhṛkuṭī-mudrā.

Regarding the method for binding the Bhṛkuṭī-ground, according to the Bhṛkuṭī-ground-binding method of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one crosses the middle fingers and those below them on both hands backward.
Place the right hand over the left with the palms facing upward;
the backs of the fingers press against the palms.
Align the two thumbs side by side, supporting one another, and extend them straight upward.
Bend the two index fingers so that their nails touch with the backs facing each other.
Support [the posture] with the two thumbs against the ground and perform the mantra-binding (*mudrā*).
Recite: *Oṃ vaśīkuru hūṃ*. This is to be recited according to the sequence of the sūtra for those of superior, middling, and inferior faculties.
This rite does not conclude with the completion of the recitation;
by reciting this mantra, all wise ones shall attain great peace and happiness,
and the acquisition of food will certainly be accomplished.
All necessities for wealth and honor shall be fully provided.
All Buddhas of the three periods who appear in the world have preached this dhāraṇī.
This dhāraṇī must not be spoken of recklessly; if it is revealed in secret at the wrong time, its efficacious power will all disperse.
Therefore, delusion cannot be transmitted;
it can only be attained through the Ācārya.
If it were not so transmitted, [it would not arise].
Both oneself and others will fall together into the three miserable realms.
Without discriminating between pure and impure, the recitation is performed as listed above.
If [the recitation] is performed within the womb of a woman...
However, if one recites it, a great efficacy will surely be achieved.
When reciting, one should contemplate the form of the Holy Cintāmaṇicakra Bodhisattva as one’s eternal refuge.
Whether man or woman, if one binds the mind in mindfulness and recites this mantra, [the result will be attained].
One should recite it during the final watch of the night and also in the early morning before eating,
either one thousand or one hundred and eight times, according to one's preference as to the number,
neither increasing nor decreasing.
If one recites it thirteen thousand times,
one shall behold all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Great Compassionate Honored Ones.
Among all mantras, this mantra is the most honored and supreme.
The merit of reciting it even once is already immense;
how much more so if one recites it daily?
That merit is inconceivable.
If one reaches one hundred thousand recitations,
both worldly and supramundane accomplishments will be fully realized;
whatever wealth, treasures, grain, or fruits one seeks in this present life will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
If one wishes to accomplish all that is loved and cherished by others,
one should likewise recite this one thousand times every day.
In the present life, one’s physical body will enter the first stage of the bodhisattva grounds, attaining complete mastery and integration.
One will swiftly encounter all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas and quickly attain perfect enlightenment (sambodhi).
This concludes the recorded method for painting images.
If there are sentient beings who recite this mantra,
they should paint an image;
in the pigments used, one must never add glue.
Use only the resin of frankincense as glue.
The person who paints the image shall observe the eight precepts of the fast.
The form of the Bodhisattva should be fashioned in the likeness of one engaged in meditative contemplation.
He has six arms;
his upper left hand forms the gesture of the golden wheel,
and his middle left hand holds a lotus flower.
The lower hand presses down upon the mountain;
the right hand forms the *dhyāna-mudrā*;
the middle hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*).
In his lower hand he holds a rosary;
he sits upon a thirty-two-petaled lotus with his right foot [extended],
and atop his head is a transformation Buddha.
With the marks and signs fully perfected, he rides upon a lunar disc;
his majestic light shines brilliantly like the radiance within the moon.
Furthermore, on the right side, paint an image of the Great Vidyārāja Hayagrīva in a wrathful form.
His majestic radiance blazes forth, and his marks and signs are perfectly complete.
His upper teeth hang downward.
The painted image may be made of any size as desired.

The Ritual Manual for Recitation: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; the Dharma of the Various Honored Ones according to the practice of both realms, which accords with the mind of the practitioner.

However, regarding the fact that among the fivefold manifestation of the body (*pañcakāyābhisambodhi*) of the Vajradhātu, I am the Lotus Body (*padmakāya*), which is the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (*Cintāmaṇicakra*):
although it is true that one class from among the five families is singled out here, might there not be an underlying intention in designating me as the Lotus Body?

Furthermore, because the *Ārya-mañjuśrī-vidyā-rāja-sādhana* (the Ritual Manual of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel) by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi is based on the *Vajradhātu*, the practitioner should face west, and so forth;
even if it relies on the *Vajradhātu*, one must not perform the Great Rite (*mahāvidhi*).
One who practices such distinct dharmas may cultivate the method of samādhi.
One who relies on the stage of the *garbha* (womb-matrix) cultivates the method of following practice (*anuprayoga*).
However, for one who practices alone in a separate location, they should perform the five repentances by chanting the *Vajradhātu* and cultivate their practice according to the eighteen paths.
The eighteen paths are the ritual procedures for sublime accomplishment.
Those who do not know this treat them with contempt and even mock them;

nevertheless, the ritual manuals of the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra rely upon these eighteen paths. One should keep them strictly secret. Regarding the section on the mudrās of the principal deity: as a preliminary to all dharmas, one first binds the Mahāvairocana mudrā and recites the five-syllable mantra.
Next is the binding of the mudrā of the principal deity of the occasion.
This involves first abiding in the Dharma-realm palace of Mahāvairocana, and then,
in accordance with the donor’s aspirations, giving rise to the great compassionate vow.
The meaning of the transformation body of the Honzon manifesting at the time of leaving the hall is that it fulfills the heart's wishes of the patron;
this is a great secret oral transmission.
It is the mantra to be applied with focused mind during the homa.
That is to say:

Oṃ jñānamoṣṭhadmani jvala hūṃ caṇḍāmaṇi. This is the King of Wish-Fulfilling Wheels (Cintāmaṇicakra). As for the faces of the principal deity, one may rely upon all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajras according to the rites for pacifying calamities (*śāntika*) and so forth.
However, regarding this dharma, it is appropriate for the practitioner who relies upon it to proceed toward the west;

many former masters have practiced according to this direction. Thus, the Vajra-son [Vajrasattva] arose. *Note: "興然" (xìngrán) is interpreted here as a transcription of the name Vajrasattva (金剛薩埵), though the character "然" (rán) may also function as a particle indicating the state of arising.*
